title: Benedict pilgrim guest nested admission and consent conditions
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Rule of Benedict chapter 61 composes guest conduct, criticism mode, worthiness, desire for stability, and consent from a known monastery. A finite evaluator distinguishes quiet guest, reasonable humble critic, exacting/vicious guest, worthy applicant, and external monk without consent. The outputs are GUEST, REVIEW, ADMIT_HIGHER_RANK, or ASK_LEAVE; a nearest-condition or unconditional-admission rival changes the source consequences.

source.work: Regula Benedicti, chapter 61, De monachis peregrinis qualiter suscipiantur
source.source_span: Complete bounded chapter 61: receive a content non-disruptive pilgrim; let the abbot assess reasonable humble criticism; deny and ask an exacting/vicious guest to leave; receive a worthy applicant seeking stability and potentially rank him higher; require the known monastery's consent or letter before accepting one of its monks.
source.provenance: The linked Latin Wikisource text contains chapter 61 immediately after chapters 58–60. This card uses the source rule structure, not a claim about a target monastic vocabulary.

duplicate_screen.checked: IDEA000335 Rule of Benedict chapter 43 fault/demotion/re-entry; IDEA000361 permission-debt card; IDEA000446 Pliny policy cursor; route-check nested admission/condition.
duplicate_screen.difference: Chapter 61 is a guest-status and external-consent classifier with a nested rank decision. It does not reuse chapter 43's late-arrival penance or a general permission-debt operator.

operators: DECIDE_GUEST(origin, conduct, criticism, worthy, wants_stability) -> ADMISSION_RESULT
rules: First reject a monk from a known monastery when consent or a commendatory letter is absent.
Otherwise ask an exacting or vicious guest to leave.
Otherwise a reasonable humble criticism opens abbot REVIEW; if the guest is worthy and seeks stability, the result can be ADMIT_HIGHER_RANK.
Otherwise content and non-disruptive conduct yields GUEST, or ADMIT_ORDINARY_RANK when stability is requested without the higher-rank condition.
constructor.rival: NEAREST_CONDITION applies only the last observed conduct flag and therefore admits the external monk or a vicious guest if the prior content flag was true; ALWAYS_ADMIT erases both expulsion and consent gates.
constructor.observable_consequence: Changing only consent, conduct, or worthiness changes the final status while the guest identity remains fixed. In particular, a worthy pilgrim can receive a higher rank, while the same apparent guest frame without external consent is denied before rank is evaluated.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if rank can be assigned before the external-consent gate, if a reasonable humble criticism has no review state, or if the same conduct flags yield contradictory results without a source reset. The source leaves the exact rank scale unspecified.
constructor.target_binding_limit: No target guest, consent marker, or rank word is independently identified.
